why: Screening and panel discussion about Mierle Laderman Ukeles and her Maintenance Art practice.

name: Scientific Controversies No. 37: Octopus Umwelt
why: Panel on octopus intelligence and consciousness with marine biologist Alex Schnell and evolutionary biologist Caroline Albertin, hosted by Janna Levin; cuttlefish on display before and after.

name: The Downtown Festival: Little Miss Sun Sign + Q&A
why: Screening of Little Miss Sun Sign, a meditation on synchronicity and manic episodes, followed by a Q&A with director Joey Frank.

name: Cora Dance Brooklyn: Pay-What-You-Can Classes

why: Weekly pay-what-you-can dance classes for ages 7 to adult starting Oct 13, with performance opportunities throughout the season.

why: Five concert pianists circulate among three technology-enhanced grand pianos to premiere a new composition by Matthias Kriesberg in homage to Alexander Scriabin.

name: Machine Girl Halloween
why: Halloween Eve electronic hardcore show with Machine Girl, with support from Deli Girls and yesterdayneverhappened.

name: Censored Chapters, Exposed Couture: Banned Books Week Fashion Show
why: Banned Books Week fashion show featuring couture inspired by banned and challenged books, presented by D'Marsh Couture.

why: Panel on tamizdat—manuscripts smuggled out of the Soviet Union—with scholars from the Tamizdat Project exploring Cold War censorship.

name: Sounds of Cyprus Presents Dialects
why: Grammy-nominated musician Peter Douskalis leads a multilingual concert exploring Greek-Cypriot, Turkish-Cypriot, and Maronite-Cypriot musical traditions.

name: Houdini: Preserving a Legacy of Magic, Escapes, and Showmanship
why: Centennial celebration of Houdini's death featuring rare archival items, conversation with escape artist Dorothy Dietrich, and a live performance by escape artist Thomas Solomon.

name: TechConnect Masterclass: Jam & Learn with Ableton Educators
why: Free all-day workshop with Ableton Certified Trainers featuring keynote presentations, jam sessions, live performances, and interactive sessions on music production software.

name: Home to Harlem: Celebrating Black Bibliography at the Schomburg Center
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
why: Half-day symposium with archivists and scholars tracing items in Arturo Schomburg's personal library, with behind-the-scenes looks at the Home to Harlem research project.

name: Halloween Happy Hour with Tim Gunn
why: Annual Halloween costume parade and contest judged by Tim Gunn; come dressed as a beloved book character, poem, or author.

name: Docent-led Gallery Tour: Revolutionary Women
why: Docent-led guided tour of the Revolutionary Women gallery exhibition.

name: Docent-led Gallery Tour: Revolutionary Women
why: Docent-led guided tour of the Revolutionary Women gallery exhibition.

name: Docent-led Gallery Tour: Democracy Matters
why: Docent-led guided tour of the Democracy Matters gallery exhibition.

name: Grand Central Terminal In-Person Tour
why: MAS docent-led architectural and historical tour of Grand Central Terminal, mostly indoors.

name: North Williamsburg In-Person Tour
why: MAS guided architectural and neighborhood walking tour of North Williamsburg with guide Zack Rhodes.

name: SoHo Cast Iron Historic District Tour
why: MAS guided tour of SoHo's cast iron architecture with architectural historian Anthony W. Robins.

name: OHNY Weekend Launch Party at the Woolworth Building
why: OHNY Weekend's official kickoff party on the 26th floor of the Woolworth Building, with music, bites from Momofuku and Russ & Daughters, and a live stone carving demo.

name: OHNY Weekend 2026
why: Annual citywide open architecture festival giving access to 300+ buildings and spaces across all five boroughs, Oct 16–18.

name: OHNY Port Infrastructure Boat Tour
why: Guided boat tour during OHNY Weekend exploring New York's working port and maritime infrastructure; departs Pier 83 Midtown.

name: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
time: varies (weekends: music and crafts; Nov 1: parade)
why: Día de los Muertos celebration through Nov 2 with calaveras, a Catrina sculpture, community ofrenda, weekend music and crafts, and a parade on Nov 1.

name: Flower Power at NYBG
why: Hippie-culture exhibition through Oct 18 with Andy Warhol's Flowers, psychedelic flower displays, and 1960s photography inside the Haupt Conservatory and grounds.

name: NYBG Farmers Market
why: Weekly outdoor farmers market with fresh produce, baked goods, and artisanal items, every Wednesday through Oct 21.

name: Growing America Exhibition
why: Exhibition through Oct 18 exploring 250 years of American history through plants and food, with historical documents and living displays of heritage crops.

name: Landscape Design Portfolios Lecture Series
why: Three-part lecture series with renowned landscape architects on honoring the past and building resilience; first lecture Oct 13, then Oct 27 and Nov 10.

name: NYBG 5K Fun Run
why: Annual 5K run through the Botanical Garden's scenic grounds and architecture, supporting biodiversity conservation work.

name: Kiku: Spotlight on Tradition
why: Display of Japanese chrysanthemums trained over 11 months into elaborate shapes including the ozukuri 'thousand bloom' style; opens Oct 31.

name: Handcrafted Horrors Film Series
price: General admission; members free for some
why: Month-long Halloween horror film series celebrating practical effects and creature design: Fantasia, Faust, Nosferatu (with live music), Bram Stoker's Dracula, The Exorcist, and more.

name: Internet Walk with Ingrid Burrington
why: Author Ingrid Burrington (Networks of New York) leads a free outdoor walk tracing the physical infrastructure of the internet through Astoria, with a book signing.

name: The Adventures of Prince Achmed (35mm) — 100th Anniversary
why: 100th anniversary 35mm screening of Lotte Reiniger's 1926 feature-length silhouette-animation masterpiece, with live musical accompaniment and a pre-show lecture.

name: In the Mouth of Madness (35mm)
why: John Carpenter's Lovecraftian meta-horror starring Sam Neill screens in 35mm as part of Handcrafted Horrors.

name: Two Films Maudit with J. Hoberman: Southland Tales + Peeping Tom
why: Critic J. Hoberman presents Richard Kelly's Southland Tales (35mm) and Michael Powell's Peeping Tom—two films loathed on release and now reappraised—with book signing.

name: Muppets Tonight: 30th Anniversary Panel & Tribute to Arthur Novell
why: Dave Goelz, Bill Barretta, and Leslie Carrara-Rudolph reunite to celebrate Muppets Tonight's 30th anniversary and pay tribute to its creator Arthur Novell.

name: Fall Yoga at MoMI with The Yoga Room
why: Free one-hour yoga class inside the museum, followed by café time and optional gallery visits; offered Oct 11 and 18.

name: The Exorcist Screening
why: Screening of the 1973 William Friedkin horror classic, in conjunction with the Horrible Sites makeup/production design exhibit in Behind the Screen.

name: MoMI Merch Meet — Artisan Market
why: First-ever MoMI artisan market featuring local makers selling art, hats, shirts, buttons, jewelry, toys, zines, comics, and housewares celebrating the moving image.

name: Pumpkin Point at Governors Island
price: Free; ferry $5 round-trip (free before 11 AM on weekends)
why: Governors Island's annual pumpkin patch in historic Nolan Park with thousands of pumpkins to pick, trick-or-treating, ghost tours, folk music by Porch Stomp, pumpkin painting, and food vendors.

name: Holy Ground: The Oyster
why: Event exploring the history and ecology of oysters in New York Harbor, in collaboration with the Billion Oyster Project.

name: Bebop Porú at Six Coasts
venue: Six Coasts by Smorgasburg, Governors Island
why: Evening dance music event at Six Coasts on Governors Island.

name: Cake Picnic 5K Run
why: 5K run on Governors Island capped off with a picnic and cake.

name: Flagpole Piñata Party
why: Giant piñata party at Governors Island's historic flagpole.

name: Reimagining Filipino Brooklyn
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Talk and short film screening exploring the now-erased Filipino waterfront community near the Brooklyn Navy Yard in the 1940s, with historian Michael Salgarolo and filmmaker Claro de los Reyes.

name: Brooklyn Trivia Night with The Trivia Masters
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Brooklyn history trivia evening with Chris Kelley and Stuart Post of The Trivia Masters, featuring tough questions, lateral-thinking games, and multimedia; solo attendees welcome.

name: Haunted Brooklyn: Ghosts, Folklore, and the Stories We Tell
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Panel on Brooklyn ghost lore and the gothic imagination with Andrea Janes (Boroughs of the Dead), horror theorist Leila Taylor, Colin Dickey (Ghostland), and novelist Victor LaValle.

name: Armed Objects: Weapons, Ornamentation, and Museum Stewardship
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: Panel on the ethics of displaying historic firearms and weapons in museums, with Cooper Hewitt chief curator Michelle Millar Fisher and arms conservator Lola Page.

name: Forgotten History: The Brooklyn Theater Fire of 1876
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont Street
why: 150th anniversary event examining the 1876 Brooklyn Theatre fire (nearly 300 dead) from two angles: Arthur Scinta's research reconstruction and Melanie Gall's perspective on performer Kate Claxton.

name: 2026 Louis Auchincloss Prize Honoring Colson Whitehead
venue: Museum of the City of New York (MCNY), 1220 Fifth Avenue
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: MCNY presents the Louis Auchincloss Prize to two-time Pulitzer Prize–winner Colson Whitehead in conversation with NYT critic Wesley Morris.

name: Halloween Bash: Ghosts of New York
venue: Museum of the City of New York, 1220 Fifth Avenue
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: Annual MCNY Halloween Bash with drag performances, costume contest (come as the ghost of a famous New Yorker), DJ Misbehaviour on the South Terrace, and themed cocktails.

name: MCNY Free Late-Night Wednesdays
time: Every Wednesday through 9 PM; pop-up bar 5–9 PM
venue: Museum of the City of New York, 1220 Fifth Avenue
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: Free Wednesday evening admission through year-end with extended 9 PM closing and a pop-up bar from 5–9 PM to explore all current exhibitions.

name: Kramer/Fauci at St. Ann's Warehouse
source: Museum of the City of New York
why: Daniel Fish directs this staging of the explosive real-life confrontation between playwright-activist Larry Kramer and Dr. Anthony Fauci at the height of the AIDS crisis; through Oct 24.

name: Art of Manga at Brooklyn Museum
why: First major manga exhibition in the Americas, featuring work from Inuyasha, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Ōoku, ONE PIECE, and more—exploring manga as a serious art form.

name: You Should Be Dancing: New York, 1976 and Beyond
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Major exhibition on NYC's 1970s-80s underground music explosion—punk, disco, hip hop—featuring CBGB's awning, Ramones/Blondie/Talking Heads guitars, Grandmaster Flash's turntables, Studio 54 memorabilia, and more.

name: Irish Literature: History & Myth Since 1798
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Exhibition tracing the arc of Irish literary culture from the 1798 United Irishmen uprising through the present, with rare manuscripts, first editions, and personal effects.

name: Halloween Fest at Fort Greene Park
why: Annual outdoor Halloween fest with costume parade, spooky stories, face painting, haunted music, and games for all ages.

name: Black History & Culture Tour of Fort Greene
venue: Fort Greene Park (meet at DeKalb Ave/Washington Park corner)
why: Guided tour tracing Fort Greene's Black History Makers and Cultural Giants route, led by local historian Suzanne Spellen, from the 1800s to today.

name: Fort Greene Artisans Bazaar
venue: Fort Greene Park (DeKalb Ave between Oxford St and Washington Park)
why: Weekly Saturday market with 30+ local designers and artisans selling upcycled fashion, handmade jewelry, small-batch apothecary, candles, local food, and more.

name: Yoga in the Park with Shala Yoga
why: Free outdoor vinyasa class at Fort Greene Park every Saturday through Oct 24, all levels welcome; bring your own mat.

name: Run Club with Chelsea Piers Fitness at Fort Greene Park
why: Weekly 3-5 mile Tuesday run starting at Fort Greene Park's monument, led by Coach Skye Massey; all paces welcome, through Nov 3.

name: Prison Ship Martyrs Memorial Commemoration
why: Solemn wreath-laying ceremony by the Sons of the American Revolution honoring patriots who died on British prison ships during the Revolution, with color guard in period uniforms.

name: BRIC JazzFest 2026
why: Two-night jazz festival with Arturo O'Farrill and the Afro Latin Jazz Orchestra, Bilal, Takuya Kuroda, Braxton Cook, Mohini Dey, Marcus Gilmore, and after-hours parties.

name: UPRISING/DOWNFALL: Repression and Resistance in the Making of Democracy
venue: Brooklyn Public Library Central Branch, 10 Grand Army Plaza
why: Late-night teach-in with live DJ set from DJ Kofta, keynote by physicist Karmela Padavic-Callaghan and Living Colour guitarist Vernon Reid, plus speakers on democratic movements, civil rights, and resistance.

name: BBG Fall Plant Sale
venue: Brooklyn Botanic Garden, Steinberg Visitor Center (990 Washington Ave)
why: Annual BBG plant sale with native trees and shrubs, unusual orchids, tropicals, succulents, and uncommon indoor and outdoor bulbs; garden admission free for shoppers.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026: Home Sweet Home
venue: Andrew Freedman Home, 1125 Grand Concourse, The Bronx
why: Annual Arch League costume ball at the beaux-arts Andrew Freedman Home in the Bronx, themed 'Home Sweet Home,' with DJs Bojaq and Madre Guia and a site-specific installation by TAKK.

name: Tenement Museum: Democracy Evening Tours
why: Evening tours with refreshments at the Tenement Museum tracing how ordinary New Yorkers advanced American democracy—from the 1870 15th Amendment parade to the 1974 Aspira bilingual education case and 1982 garment strikes; next dates Oct 13 and Nov 12.

name: Ancestral Ecologies Archtober Sunset Tour
why: Archtober sunset tour of 'Ancestral Ecologies,' four multisensory installations by Olalekan Jeyifous and AD--WO exploring Afrodiasporic and Latinx approaches to ecological stewardship; exhibition closes Oct 25.

name: BBG Lightscape 2026
why: Annual illuminated nighttime trail through the Garden with new light installations themed around the four seasons of the Garden's splendor; runs select dates through Jan 3, 2027.

name: Nowicki's Unbuilt Chandigarh: An Ecology of Everyday Life
why: Talk on Polish-American architect Maciej Nowicki's visionary unbuilt designs for Chandigarh, India—imagining what could have been—in conjunction with the 'Humanist modernity' exhibition.

name: J. Max Bond Jr. Lecture and Portrait Unveiling
why: Lecture honoring J. Max Bond Jr.—pioneering architect whose work includes the National September 11 Memorial Museum and Schomburg Center renovation—with unveiling of his portrait.

name: Beyond Code: Designing for Resilience, Risk, and the Future Standard of Care
why: Panel discussion on how climate resilience and environmental performance are reshaping architectural practice and professional standards of care.

name: Eating Through Streetscapes: Food, Frontage, and Public Space
why: Discussion on the intersection of food culture, street frontage, and the design of NYC's public spaces—how restaurants and vendors shape the experience of the city.

name: Walking Tour: Madison Avenue, High Fashion, and Historic Preservation
venue: Madison Avenue (meeting point TBD, see registration)
why: Archtober walking tour of Madison Avenue exploring the tension between luxury retail architecture, historic preservation, and the buildings that define the Gold Coast.

name: Exhibition Tour: Humanist Modernity—Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki
why: Guided tour of the exhibition on the visionary Polish-American architects Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki, whose careers bridged modernism and humanism before Maciej's death in 1950.

name: Walking Tour: The Rise of the Skyscraper in Downtown New York
venue: Downtown Manhattan (meeting point TBD, see registration)
why: Archtober walking tour tracing the architectural history of the skyscraper in lower Manhattan, from early cast-iron buildings to the 20th-century towers that defined the skyline.

name: Archtober x ADFF: Architecture & Design Film Festival Short Films
why: Four-hour showcase of short films from the Architecture & Design Film Festival (ADFF), presented as part of Archtober—architecture documentaries, design fiction, and experimental film.

name: Humanist Modernity: Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki (Exhibition)
why: Major exhibition on Polish-American architects Maciej and Stanisława Nowicki, whose humanist modernism—bridging Bauhaus principles with cultural sensitivity—influenced a generation of designers.

name: Dark Matter U: Justice, Pedagogy, Design (Exhibition)
why: Exhibition exploring how architecture education can center justice and equity, featuring work from students, educators, and practitioners rethinking design pedagogy.

name: Why Design? (Exhibition)
why: Exhibition asking foundational questions about design's purpose and impact, featuring diverse perspectives from architects, educators, and communities on what design is for.

name: Through the Mirror: Homelessness, Healthcare, and Innovation in the NYC Subways
venue: NY Transit Museum, Boerum Place & Schermerhorn St
why: Panel discussion moderated by Elizabeth Glazer (Vital City) on how homelessness and healthcare intersect on the subway, featuring the MTA and city partners on new co-response programs.

name: NYC Secrets and Lies: Transit Tales
venue: NY Transit Museum, Boerum Place & Schermerhorn St
why: Interactive transit-themed edition of NYC's Secrets & Lies game night—separate fact from fiction about transit lore; identify the liar and win tickets to an NYTM walking tour.

name: Underground NYC Tour: Subway 101
why: Expert-guided subway tour visiting old and new stations, exploring subway art and architecture, with exclusive archival images from the NYTM collection; next dates Oct 9, Oct 24, Nov 12.

name: Transit Walk: Downtown Brooklyn
why: Walking tour tracing Downtown Brooklyn's transit history from early ferry landings and trolley routes through the elevated train and subway era, ending at the historic Court Street Station.

name: Transit Walk: Gowanus and Carroll Gardens
why: Transit history walking tour of Gowanus and Carroll Gardens, examining how transit shaped two of Brooklyn's most transformed neighborhoods.

name: Transit Walk: Art and Design Secrets of Penn Station & Moynihan Train Hall
time: 11:00 AM (also Dec 16 at 11 AM and 2 PM)
why: Walking tour revealing hidden architectural remnants of the demolished Beaux-Arts Penn Station and new public artworks in Moynihan Train Hall.

name: Fly Away Redbirds Nostalgia Ride
venue: Old South Ferry Station (1905), departs Manhattan
why: Round-trip excursion to the Bronx on the legendary Redbird subway cars (1959–2003), departing from the historic Old South Ferry station—closed to the public since 2017.

name: Subway Swing: A Boogie for the Ages
venue: NY Transit Museum, Boerum Place & Schermerhorn St
why: After-hours swing dance party in the 1936 decommissioned subway station, with live jazz bands, the hottest swing dancing, and vintage-inspired dress encouraged.

name: Matías Duville: Monitor Yin Yang Book Launch
why: Launch of Argentine artist Matías Duville's trilingual travel guide 'Monitor Yin Yang' (Spanish/English/Italian) with 50 drawings, a photo album, and a fold-out map; conversation with Michel Nieva and Josefina Barcia.

name: K8 Hardy: Positions Book Launch
why: Launch of K8 Hardy's 'Positions,' collecting all 50 photographs from her pathbreaking Position Series (2007–12) on queer identity, DIY fashion, and early-2000s New York subcultures, with previously unseen images.

name: Insider Trading II: A Candid Publishing Panel
why: Off-the-record panel on the anatomy of publishing with Steff Yotka (Editor-in-Chief of i-D), Yusuf Hassan (BlackMass Publishing), and Academy Award-nominated costume designer Miyako Bellizzi.

name: Rong Xin: Roaming a Flushing Mall Book Launch
why: Book launch for 'Rong Xin,' translating the 2023 exhibition 'Home-O-Stasis: Life and Livelihoods in Flushing' at Rong Xin Plaza into print; panel with designer Sixuan Tong, editor Michael Guo, moderated by curator Herb Tam.

name: Nina Katchadourian: Seat Assignment Book Discussion
why: Discussion of Nina Katchadourian's 11-year project making art on airplanes using only in-flight materials—documented in hundreds of photographs of her seat-tray creations.

name: RisoLAB Talks vol. 5: Travess Smalley & Kyle Canyon
why: Artists Travess Smalley and Kyle Canyon discuss their Riso-printed works-in-residence, with Smalley's experimental fluorescent Quadrifluox tabloid prints and Canyon's pop-surrealist comic 'Gauche Neapolitain Girl'; closing reception with works for sale.

name: Lower East Side Printshop OHNY Open House
time: Fri Oct 16 12–6 PM; Sat Oct 17 12–4 PM (with 1 PM screenprinting & 3 PM linocut demos)
venue: Lower East Side Printshop, 306 W. 37th St, 6th Floor (enter from 307 W. 36th St)
why: OHNY Weekend open studio at one of NYC's flagship community printmaking spaces, with studio tours, gallery exhibition, artist studio visits, plus live screenprinting and linoleum-cut demos on Saturday.

name: LESP x Print Center NY: Copper Etching Intensive
venue: Lower East Side Printshop, 306 W. 37th St, 6th Floor
why: Intensive copper etching workshop at LESP in conjunction with the Parasol Press exhibition at Print Center New York; also offered Nov 7.

name: LESP x Morgan Library: Intaglio Etching Workshop
venue: Lower East Side Printshop, 306 W. 37th St, 6th Floor
why: Intaglio etching workshop at LESP linked to the Morgan Library's exhibition 'Rembrandt's Lions: Art and Exile in the Dutch Republic'—learn the technique Rembrandt mastered.

name: Night at the Haunted Opera: Best New Horror 2026
price: Free (free book giveaway while supplies last)
why: Authors Deena Helm, Saratoga Schaefer, and Kailee Pedersen (who is also an opera singer) discuss the year's buzziest horror books with librarian Becky Spratford, followed by a live performance.

name: Censored Chapters, Exposed Couture: A Banned Books Week Fashion Show
venue: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library (SNFL), 455 Fifth Ave
why: Fashion show featuring couture looks inspired by banned books, designed by award-winning Jamaican-born NY designer Glenroy March (House of D'Marsh), with giveaways.

name: Banned Books from the Cold War to the Present
venue: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library (SNFL), 455 Fifth Ave
why: Yasha Klots of the Tamizdat Project discusses manuscripts smuggled out from behind the Iron Curtain—'tamizdat,' or 'published over there'—and their enduring power.

name: Kerry Kennedy with Douglas Brinkley: The Bold and Extraordinary Ethel Kennedy
venue: NYPL Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, 5th Ave & 42nd St
why: Kerry Kennedy discusses her biography of Ethel Kennedy with presidential historian Douglas Brinkley, drawing on family memories and her mother's private papers.

name: TechConnect Masterclass: Jam & Learn with Ableton
venue: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library (SNFL), 455 Fifth Ave
why: Full day of Ableton learning with Certified Trainers: keynote presentations, jam sessions, live performances, and interactive breakout sessions for musicians, producers, and educators.

name: Home to Harlem: Celebrating Black Bibliography at the Schomburg
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, 515 Malcolm X Blvd
why: Half-day symposium with archivists and scholars on Black bibliography, with behind-the-scenes look at how Arturo Schomburg's personal library was identified; tied to the Schomburg Center's Centennial.

name: Black on Screen: Honoring Marlon Riggs
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, 515 Malcolm X Blvd
why: Screening of Marlon Riggs's 1993 short 'Non, Je Ne Regrette Rien (No Regret)'—five HIV-positive gay Black men on living with AIDS—followed by a conversation on Riggs's legacy with Dr. Gervais Marsh and Sur Rodney (Sur).

name: NYPL Halloween Happy Hour
why: NYPL's popular annual Halloween party featuring a costume parade judged by Tim Gunn and NYPL librarians.

name: NYPL/WNYC Get Lit Book Club: Whidbey by T Kira Madden
why: NYPL and WNYC's Get Lit Book Club discussion of T Kira Madden's debut novel 'Whidbey,' with WNYC host Alison Stewart.

name: Winnie-the-Pooh at 100 Anniversary Display
venue: NYPL Polonsky Exhibition of the NYPL's Treasures, 476 Fifth Ave
why: Centennial display marking the 100th anniversary of Winnie-the-Pooh (first published Oct 1926), with original A. A. Milne mockups, Shepard illustrations, translations, and for the first time on public display the new Roo toy gifted by Queen Camilla.

name: Pioneer Works Supper Club: Pierce Abernathy on Marine Foodways
why: Dinner by chef and slow-food advocate Pierce Abernathy centered on oceanic ingredients and marine foodways, with a screening of Abernathy's short film on alternative seafood and farming solutions across NYC; presented with Off The Table.

name: Pioneer Works Second Sundays: Ocean Season
why: Monthly open house featuring live dwarf cuttlefish with scientist Tessa Montague, community seaweed science with Seaweed City, a screening of Jean Painlevé's 1967 The Love Life of the Octopus, LaJuné McMillian installation walkthrough, artist open studios, and the launch of Marlon James's new novel The Disappearers with Colin Channer; Ragga NYC's Neon Christina closes the night.

name: Scientific Controversies No. 37: Octopus Umwelt
why: Director of Sciences Janna Levin hosts comparative psychologist Dr. Alex Schnell and evolutionary biologist Dr. Caroline Albertin on octopus consciousness, memory, and what these creatures can teach us about intelligence.

name: Tuomas A. Laitinen: Siphon (Exhibition)
venue: Pioneer Works Main Hall, 159 Pioneer St
why: Immersive 8K video installation exploring octopus consciousness through kaleidoscopic footage of octopus camouflage patterns from an Okinawa research lab, alongside blown-glass sculptures in water tanks arranged by 86-year-old Japanese ikebana master Kosen Ohtsubo, and a 'tentacular' spatial audio work filling the three-story Main Hall.

name: LaJuné McMillian: Child/ren of the Bloom (Exhibition)
venue: Pioneer Works 3rd Floor Gallery, 159 Pioneer St
why: Interactive installation responding to visitors' movements with floor-to-ceiling video transforming research on phytoplankton and bioluminescence into a spiritual encounter with oceanic systems; developed from an OceanX Education artist residency.

name: Abandoned Railway Urban Hike: Forest Park & the Future QueensWay
venue: Forest Park, Queens (meeting point per registration)
why: Guided hike exploring the abandoned LIRR Rockaway Beach Branch rail corridor through Forest Park, with insight into the QueensWay proposal to convert it into a linear park.

name: NYAC: The Secret Eats of Arthur Avenue Food Crawl
venue: Arthur Avenue, the Bronx (meeting point per registration)
why: Guided food crawl through the Bronx's Arthur Avenue neighborhood—NYC's 'real Little Italy'—visiting old-school Italian delis, bakeries, and pasta makers with a local expert.

name: NYAC: Inside The Players Club with Rare Look Inside Edwin Booth's Bedroom
venue: The Players Club, 16 Gramercy Park South
why: Exclusive access to The Players, the historic private club founded by actor Edwin Booth in 1888 on Gramercy Park, including a rare look inside Booth's preserved bedroom—closed to the public since his death in 1893.

name: NYAC: Behind-the-Scenes at Lincoln Center Extended Tour
why: Extended behind-the-scenes tour of Lincoln Center going beyond the standard public areas, exploring backstage spaces and architectural history of Alice Tully Hall, the Met Opera, and Avery Fisher Hall.

name: NYAC: From Crypt to Roof — After-Hours Tour of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine
venue: Cathedral of St. John the Divine, Amsterdam Ave & 112th St
why: After-hours access to the world's largest Gothic cathedral, from the crypt beneath the main floor to rooftop views of Manhattan—most of these spaces are not accessible to the general public.

name: NYAC: Exclusive Truffle Pasta Making at The Urbani Truffle Lab NYC
why: Hands-on truffle pasta-making experience at the Urbani Truffle Lab, NYC's premier truffle importer, with expert guidance on pairing, preparation, and tasting.

name: NYAC: Inside the Society of Illustrators: Norman Rockwell to Archives
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of the Society of Illustrators (founded 1901) including the original Norman Rockwell painting hanging in the building and access to their archives.

name: NYAC: Grave Robbers of New York — Exploring the City's Body Snatching History
why: Halloween-season walking tour tracing NYC's 19th-century grave-robbing history—when medical schools paid for fresh cadavers and 'resurrection men' prowled cemeteries at night.

name: NYAC: Exclusive Trip Inside the Loew's Valencia — NYC's First Wonder Theatre
venue: Loew's Valencia Theatre, 165-11 Jamaica Ave, Jamaica Queens
why: Rare access to the Loew's Valencia (1929), one of the original five atmospheric 'Wonder Theatres' and now a Seventh-Day Adventist church that has preserved its extraordinary Spanish Baroque interior—not open to the public otherwise.

name: NYAC: After-Hours Conservation Lab Tour at the New-York Historical Society
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: After-hours access to the New-York Historical Society's brand-new conservation lab, normally off-limits to the public, to see how objects from the collection are preserved, restored, and analyzed.

name: Mathematics and the Art of M.C. Escher (Exhibition)
venue: National Museum of Mathematics (MoMath), 11 E 26th St
why: The first major exhibition devoted to the mathematics behind Escher's mind-bending works, with 60+ prints, drawings, original woodblocks, and objects exploring symmetry, geometry, infinity, and perspective.

name: 13th Annual Americas Film Festival of New York
why: Closing week of the Americas Film Festival exploring stories of historical memory, migration, identity, and music from across the Americas, with features, documentaries, shorts, and filmmaker Q&As.

name: Bhangra in the Plaza (Free, Wednesdays through Oct 21)
why: Free outdoor Bhangra dance classes in the middle of Midtown Manhattan with Sarina Jain and Masala Bhangra dancers—watch and join in; all ages and experience levels welcome, runs through Oct 21.

name: We Want to Believe: UFOs, Aliens, and Us
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont St
why: Poet and literary critic Adam Kirsch discusses his new book tracing the remarkable journey of UFOs from cultural punchline to subject of serious government investigation, drawing on declassified documents and a long history of believers and skeptics; conversation led by former Harper's editor-in-chief Christopher Beha.

name: Rebuilding American Democracy: The Path to a Functioning Government
venue: Center for Brooklyn History, 128 Pierrepont St
why: Legal scholar and former Biden administration official K. Sabeel Rahman discusses his book 'Remaking the State: A New Blueprint for American Democracy,' arguing the crisis goes beyond elections to the institutions of government themselves; conversation with New York Times economics reporter Talmon Joseph Smith.

name: The Dark Stage: New York and the Business of Blackface
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Dr. Rhae Lynn Barnes (author of 'Darkology: Blackface and the American Way of Entertainment') examines NYC's role as global epicenter of blackface minstrelsy and how grassroots organizations led by Black mothers fought to dismantle it.

name: NY Historical Docent Tour: Revolutionary Women
venue: New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
why: Docent-led tour of the NY Historical Society galleries focusing on women's roles in the American Revolution—part of the museum's ongoing Democracy Matters programming.
